answers: Setup time is the minimum time before the clock edge that data must be stable at a flip-flop input. Violating it causes the flip-flop to capture incorrect data.
Hold time is the minimum time after the clock edge that data must remain stable. A hold violation causes the flip-flop to capture a wrong value after the clock edge.
Slack is the difference between required arrival time and actual arrival time of a signal. Positive slack means timing is met. Negative slack means a violation exists.
The critical path is the longest combinational path between two flip-flops. It determines the maximum operating frequency of the design.
Clock skew is the difference in arrival time of the clock signal at different flip-flops in the design. It can cause both setup and hold violations.
Metastability occurs when a flip-flop samples data that is changing near the clock edge. The output enters an undefined state for an unpredictable time.
Static Timing Analysis verifies timing of a digital circuit without simulation. It checks all paths to ensure signals meet setup and hold requirements.
A timing corner is a specific combination of process voltage and temperature conditions. Timing must be verified across all corners to ensure reliable operation.
A D flip-flop captures the value of its D input at the rising clock edge and holds it until the next clock edge. It is the most common storage element in digital design.

questions: What is the difference between latch and flip-flop?
answers: A latch is level-sensitive and changes output whenever the enable is active. A flip-flop is edge-triggered and only changes state on a clock edge.
A JK flip-flop has J and K inputs. J=1 K=0 sets the output. J=0 K=1 resets it. J=K=1 toggles the output.
Clock domain crossing occurs when a signal passes between two flip-flops clocked by different clocks. It can cause metastability if not handled with a synchronizer.
A synchronizer uses two flip-flops in series to reduce metastability probability in CDC paths. It increases mean time between failures but does not eliminate metastability.
An SR latch has Set and Reset inputs. S=1 sets output to 1. R=1 resets to 0. S=R=1 is an invalid state that must be avoided.
A half adder adds two single bits and produces a sum and carry output. Sum is the XOR of inputs and carry is the AND of inputs.
A full adder adds three bits including a carry-in and produces sum and carry-out. It is used to build multi-bit adders by chaining.
A multiplexer selects one of several input signals and forwards it to the output based on select lines. A 2:1 MUX has two inputs one select and one output.
A decoder converts a binary code of n bits into 2^n output lines. Exactly one output is active at a time based on the input combination.
A priority encoder takes multiple inputs and outputs the binary code of the highest priority active input. It resolves conflicts when multiple inputs are active simultaneously.
Propagation delay is the time taken for the output of a logic gate to change after a change at its input. It determines the maximum speed of a combinational circuit.
